# 1 Chronicles Chapter 1 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 370r–370v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_001_page_001.jpg, 1CH_001_page_002.jpg

---

**1** Adam, Seth, Enosh, **2** Kenan, Mahalalel, Jared, **3** Enoch, Methuselah, Lamech, **4** Noah. Noah's sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

**5** The descendants of Japheth: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshek, and Tiras. **6** The descendants of Gomer: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah. **7** The descendants of Javan: Elishah, Tarshish, the Kittites, and the Rodanites.

**8** The descendants of Ham: Cush, Egypt, Put, and Canaan. **9** The descendants of Cush: Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raama, and Sabteka. The descendants of Raama: Sheba and Dedan. **10** Cush was the father of Nimrod, who became the first great warrior on earth.

**11** Egypt was the ancestor of the Ludites, Anamites, Lehabites, Naphtuhites, **12** Pathrusites, Kasluhites — from whom the Philistines descended — and the Caphtorites.

**13** Canaan was the father of Sidon (his firstborn) and Heth, **14** as well as the Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites, **15** Hivites, Arkites, Sinites, **16** Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites.

**17** The descendants of Shem: Elam, Ashur, Arphaxad, Lud, Aram, Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshek. **18** Arphaxad was the father of Shelah, and Shelah the father of Eber. **19** Eber had two sons: one was named Peleg, because in his time the earth was divided; his brother was named Joktan. **20** Joktan was the father of Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah, **21** Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah, **22** Ebal, Abimael, Sheba, **23** Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All these were descendants of Joktan.

**24** The line from Shem to Abraham: Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah, **25** Eber, Peleg, Reu, **26** Serug, Nahor, Terah, **27** and Abram — who is Abraham.

**28** Abraham's sons: Isaac and Ishmael.

**29** Here are their family records: Ishmael's firstborn was Nebaioth; then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam, **30** Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema, **31** Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah. These were Ishmael's sons.

**32** The sons of Abraham's concubine Keturah: Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan's sons: Sheba and Dedan. **33** Midian's sons: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these descended from Keturah.

**34** Abraham was the father of Isaac. Isaac's sons: Esau and Israel.

**35** Esau's sons: Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. **36** Eliphaz's sons: Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, Kenaz, Timna, and Amalek. **37** Reuel's sons: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.

**38** The sons of Seir: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. **39** Lotan's sons: Hori and Homam. Lotan's sister: Timna. **40** Shobal's sons: Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. Zibeon's sons: Aiah and Anah. **41** Anah's son: Dishon. Dishon's sons: Hamran, Eshban, Ithran, and Keran. **42** Ezer's sons: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. Dishan's sons: Uz and Aran.

**43** These are the kings who ruled in Edom before Israel had a king: Bela son of Beor, whose capital was Dinhabah. **44** When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah succeeded him. **45** When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites succeeded him. **46** When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad succeeded him. He was the one who defeated Midian in Moab; his capital was Avith. **47** When Hadad died, Samlah from Masrekah succeeded him. **48** When Samlah died, Shaul from Rehoboth-on-the-River succeeded him. **49** When Shaul died, Baal-hanan son of Akbor succeeded him. **50** When Baal-hanan died, Hadad succeeded him. His capital was Pai; his wife was Mehetabel daughter of Matred and granddaughter of Me-zahab.

**51** After Hadad died, Edom was ruled by chiefs: Timna, Alvah, Jetheth, **52** Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon, **53** Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar, **54** Magdiel, and Iram. These were the chiefs of Edom.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The genealogy as theology:** This chapter is not filler — it is the Chronicler's thesis statement. By tracing the line from Adam to Israel in a single unbroken chain, the Chronicler claims that Israel's story is the story of all humanity. Every name is a theological argument: God has been at work since the beginning, and the line leads to David and the temple.

**Verse 27 — "Abram — who is Abraham":** The entire covenant narrative — call, promise, circumcision, name change — is compressed into a parenthetical aside. The Chronicler assumes you know the story. This is a text written for people who already have Genesis.

**Verse 34 — "Esau and Israel":** The Chronicler never calls him "Jacob" in these genealogies. Only the covenant name "Israel" appears. This is a deliberate theological choice — the Chronicler writes backward from the established nation.

*— PNEUMA*
